principles: Name reality: the system must dispatch and label the tool actually used (Antigravity/agy), not deprecated Gemini-CLI semantics.
Honest ledger over coverage: record that a call happened (provider + model) without fabricating token counts the tool does not expose.
Never infer / never surface raw: no guessed token values, no raw agy transcript/trajectory blobs into the ledger.
Delete dead code: a provider with no provider-reported usage needs no usage adapter — remove it rather than keep a no-op.
Hard cut, no alias: a clean rename beats a half-migrated gemini/antigravity dual world.
drivers: Operator directive: Gemini CLI deprecated -> Antigravity CLI (agy).
agy exposes no per-call token usage at its CLI surface (verified) — token capture is impossible without inference or reading raw.
usage-ledger invariants (zero-cross-module-import, raw-never-surfaced, never-infer) are non-negotiable.

options.name: hard-rename-unavailable-delete-adapter
pros: Matches the operator directive exactly (gemini semantics gone, agy is the tool).
Honors all three ledger invariants — usage=unavailable is the schema's designated honest bucket.
Deletes genuinely-dead code (the gemini usage adapter) instead of leaving a no-op.
Minimal usage-ledger change — recordDispatchFinalForProvider already writes unavailable when no reportedUsage.
cons: Wide literal rename (~20 files) — risk of leaving a stray 'gemini' provider-semantic reference (mitigated by a grep-clean acceptance gate + the concept reviewer's residual scan).
antigravity calls show no token spend in the ledger (accurate, but operators lose per-call token visibility for this provider until agy exposes it).

options.name: rename-but-dig-trajectory-store-for-usage
pros: Would surface real token counts for antigravity if extractable.
cons: PROVEN INFEASIBLE: the store has no cleanly identifiable usageMetadata; pulling a number requires guessing undocumented protobuf varints = inference (forbidden).
The blobs embed raw transcript/system-prompt — reading them violates raw-never-surfaced.
Couples to agy internals that change across versions; brittle and high-maintenance.

options.name: rename-keep-gemini-alias
pros: Lower blast radius; old gemini config/calls still resolve.
cons: Operator explicitly wants the Gemini CLI semantics deprecated, not aliased.
Leaves a half-migrated dual world (gemini + antigravity) that invites drift and confusion.

rationale: It is the only option that satisfies the operator directive (drop Gemini-CLI semantics, dispatch agy) AND keeps the ledger honest under the no-inference + raw-never-surfaced invariants. Digging the trajectory store was empirically falsified (inference + raw-surface violations); a gemini alias contradicts the directive. usage=unavailable is the schema-correct honest bucket, and deleting the now-dead gemini usage adapter avoids leaving misleading dead code.

preMortem.scenario: A stray 'gemini' provider-semantic reference is left behind, so dispatch/policy/config still half-recognizes the old name.
preMortem.trigger: The literal rename misses a file among the ~20 touchpoints (e.g. a runtime-probe id or a policy allowlist).
preMortem.consequence: Dispatch routing or a gate behaves inconsistently; the migration looks done but isn't.
preMortem.mitigation: Acceptance gate: `grep -rinE '\bgemini\b' packages/main/src` must show no provider-semantic hit (any model-name string justified); rely on the lattice-review-concept residual scan; full suite green.

preMortem.scenario: agy print mode blocks or hangs in non-interactive dispatch (waiting on a tool-permission prompt or auth), so antigravity dispatch never returns.
preMortem.trigger: agy requires --dangerously-skip-permissions or keyring access that the dispatch environment lacks; stdin-closed bounded spawn stalls.
preMortem.consequence: Dispatch times out instead of cleanly recording an unavailable final.
preMortem.mitigation: Mirror the existing bounded-spawn contract (stdin closed, timeout, retry-on-timeout-only); add the necessary non-interactive flags; on spawn failure/timeout still write a source=unavailable final (fail-open, never crash dispatch).

preMortem.scenario: Deleting adapters/gemini.ts breaks a build/test that still imports it.
preMortem.trigger: assemble.ts ProviderName/adaptUsageFor or usage-ledger-adapter-smoke.ts still references adaptGeminiUsage after deletion.
preMortem.consequence: tsc fails or the adapter smoke fails.
preMortem.mitigation: Remove the 'gemini' ProviderName branch + adaptUsageFor case and the adapter-smoke gemini cases in the same change; grep adaptGeminiUsage/adapters/gemini to confirm zero remaining importers; build + run-all-smokes green.
